message:
## Summary
- Complete architectural rewrite from MVC to clean architecture using modern Swift patterns
- Full migration from UIKit to SwiftUI with iOS 26 support
- Modularized codebase into separate Swift packages with clear separation of concerns

## Architecture Changes
### Package Structure
Created modular Swift packages following clean architecture principles:
- **Domain**: Core business logic, models, and use cases
- **Data**: Repository implementations and data persistence
- **Networking**: Network layer abstraction
- **Shared**: Common utilities, extensions, and dependency injection
- **DesignSystem**: Reusable UI components and theming
- **Features**: Self-contained feature modules (Feed, Comments, Settings, Onboarding)

### Key Improvements
- **Separation of Concerns**: Clear boundaries between UI, business logic, and data layers
- **Testability**: Comprehensive unit tests added for all packages (10,000+ lines of test code)
- **Dependency Injection**: Protocol-based DI container for loose coupling
- **Modern Swift**: Swift 6.2 with async/await, actors, and Swift Testing framework

## UI/UX Enhancements
### SwiftUI Migration
- Replaced all UIKit views with native SwiftUI implementations
- Modern navigation patterns using NavigationStack
- Proper iPad support with selection highlighting
- Dynamic type support with customizable text scaling (5 size options)

### Visual Improvements
- Consolidated voting system with consistent UI across Feed and Comments
- Modern vote indicators and buttons with proper color consistency
- Native SwiftUI onboarding replacing WhatsNewKit
- Updated to latest iOS 26 APIs with modern visual effects
- Proper dark mode support throughout

### Component Updates
- **PostDisplayView**: Clean SwiftUI implementation with proper link handling
- **CommentsView**: Full rewrite with thumbnail support and improved navigation
- **FeedView**: Simplified architecture with proper refresh behavior
- **SettingsView**: Modernized with iOS design standards
- **LoginView**: Updated authentication flow with proper logout handling

## Code Quality
### Testing
- Added comprehensive Swift Testing suites for all modules
- Unit tests for ViewModels, Repositories, and Use Cases
- Test coverage for critical business logic
- Proper mocking and dependency injection in tests

### Performance
- Generic LoadingStateManager for efficient data loading
- Optimized list rendering and selection behavior
- Reduced view recreation and improved navigation performance
- Proper memory management with weak references where needed

## Technical Details
### Removed Legacy Code
- Eliminated 3,400+ lines of legacy UIKit code
- Removed type bridges and NavigationView wrappers
- Cleaned up duplicate functionality
- Removed unused extensions and utilities

### Added Modern Patterns
- MVVM architecture with ObservableObject ViewModels
- Repository pattern for data access
- Use case pattern for business logic
- Protocol-oriented programming throughout

## Breaking Changes
- Minimum iOS version now targets latest (iOS 26)
- Swift 6.2 required for compilation
- Some settings removed (thumbnails, swipe actions) in favor of cleaner UX

## Testing
All tests pass successfully with the new architecture. The app has been thoroughly tested on both iPhone and iPad simulators.
